steps: Meet Maya at Brightline. On day one, she types help me with reports, and Claude returns generic structure tips. A vague prompt gets generic advice.
First, description. Maya tells her manager what Claude can do, what it cannot, and how she will review its work. It is a faster first draft, not a replacement for her review.
Next, delegation. The metrics summary goes to Claude, but the renewal risk call stays with Maya, because it is a judgment call, and she asks whether each task is reversible.
Then diligence. Her checklist runs on every output, even low-stakes ones, every day: no personal data, facts that match, and the Brightline tone.
Now discernment. Claude cites three major competitors, so Maya checks the source sheet. Only one is listed. The other two are not there.
So Maya re-prompts: use only the competitor sheet, and if one is not listed, say so. Claude regenerates the summary, limited to the sheet.
Finally, Maya hands her manager a verified summary, plus her own call on the renewal risk. That is the four Ds working together.
